title: Society Redevelopment
summary: Start with records, member priorities and a structured professional review.

sections.title: Begin with the society
sections.body: Record member objectives, known building concerns and the committee’s current mandate. Organize the existing records before evaluating promises or offers.

sections.title: Define the advisory team
sections.body: Set out the roles of the PMC, architect, engineer, lawyer and other specialists. Compare scope, independence, communication and fees.

sections.title: Make decisions on comparable information
sections.body: A common brief helps compare feasibility assumptions, developer capability, rehabilitation terms and safeguards. Keep a record of decisions and unresolved questions.

title: Self-Redevelopment
summary: Understand the control, responsibilities and risks of a society-led project.

sections.title: What changes
sections.body: The society organizes its project through appointed professionals and contractors rather than relying on a conventional developer-led arrangement.

sections.title: Evaluate capacity first
sections.body: Review member alignment, the committee’s capacity, funding requirements, procurement and delivery risks before choosing this model.

sections.title: Plan the entire cash flow
sections.body: Budget for construction, approvals, professional fees, rehabilitation, financing and contingency. Funding remains subject to lender appraisal and project viability.

title: MahaRERA
summary: Use official project records as one part of your due diligence.

sections.title: Use the official portal
sections.body: MahaRERA provides registered project searches, project information, regulatory resources and complaint-related information.

sections.title: Review the relevant record
sections.body: Match the promoter, project name and registration details. Review published information and seek clarification on gaps with a qualified adviser.

sections.title: Keep the review in context
sections.body: Registration is not a substitute for title review, technical assessment or independent contract advice. Applicability to a particular redevelopment proposal needs professional review.

title: FSI & TDR
summary: Understand development capacity without relying on a headline area promise.

sections.title: What the terms mean
sections.body: Floor Space Index relates permitted floor area to plot area under the applicable regulations. Transferable Development Rights are development rights that may be used subject to applicable conditions.

sections.title: Why site details matter
sections.body: Road access, plot conditions, reservations and the applicable planning provisions affect development potential. An architect should assess the actual site and current rules.

sections.title: Ask for the assumptions
sections.body: Request a written feasibility assessment showing the planning inputs, rehabilitation needs, costs and sensitivity to changes. Additional carpet area cannot be assumed from a generic multiplier.

title: DCPR 2034
summary: Ask how Mumbai’s development regulations apply to your specific property.

sections.title: A planning framework
sections.body: Mumbai’s Development Control and Promotion Regulations provide a framework for land use, development permissions and building requirements.

sections.title: Check the applicable provisions
sections.body: Your architect should identify the relevant provisions, site reservations, access conditions and permissions. Later notifications or amendments may affect an assessment.

sections.title: Document the conclusion
sections.body: Keep the professional assessment, planning inputs and authority correspondence in the project record. A summary on a website cannot establish a property’s entitlement.

title: Property Title Verification
summary: Organize ownership records and identify questions before commercial commitments.

sections.title: Collect the chain of records
sections.body: Begin with available conveyance, lease, land or property records and supporting transaction documents. Have a qualified lawyer determine the search scope.

sections.title: Identify gaps
sections.body: Ownership discrepancies, encumbrances, disputes and inconsistent property descriptions require specific review. A property card alone does not replace a legal title opinion.

sections.title: Coordinate resolution
sections.body: Record issues and proposed next steps. Obtain specialist advice before treating an unresolved issue as cleared or proceeding with a transaction.

title: Deemed Conveyance
summary: Understand the process and organize documents with qualified legal support.

sections.title: Why it may arise
sections.body: Where conveyance has not been completed, a society may need to examine whether a deemed conveyance application is appropriate under the applicable framework.

sections.title: Use the official process
sections.body: The Maharashtra Co-operation Department provides an online deemed conveyance system and guidance. Eligibility and documentation require case-specific legal review.

sections.title: Keep redevelopment decisions separate
sections.body: Securing or reviewing ownership documentation is part of preparation. It does not itself settle every feasibility, planning or contractual issue in a redevelopment project.

title: Developer Selection
summary: Compare delivery capability as carefully as commercial terms.

sections.title: Create a common brief
sections.body: Specify the society’s requirements and request proposals in a comparable format covering rehabilitation, specifications, schedules and responsibilities.

sections.title: Evaluate capability
sections.body: Review funding, relevant delivery history, published project information and feedback from past societies where available. Record conflicts and assumptions.

sections.title: Review protections
sections.body: Have advisers compare securities, rent arrangements, milestones, default remedies and handover obligations. No single headline benefit should decide the outcome.

title: PMC Appointment
summary: Appoint the right professional team with a defined scope.

sections.title: Compare the appointment
sections.body: Evaluate relevant experience, technical team, independence, references and fee structure. Discuss who will actually handle the assignment.

sections.title: Set out deliverables
sections.body: Agree feasibility outputs, tender support, reporting, site review responsibilities, meeting schedules and escalation processes in writing.

sections.title: Monitor the engagement
sections.body: Review progress against the agreed scope and record material changes. The society remains responsible for its own decisions with advice from its appointed specialists.

title: Redevelopment FAQs
summary: A starting point for the questions housing societies ask most often.

sections.title: Before the first meeting
sections.body: Bring available society, title, building and member records, together with a list of objectives and known concerns.

sections.title: Before comparing offers
sections.body: Ask what feasibility assumptions support the proposal, what professional reviews are complete and what remains uncertain.

sections.title: Before signing
sections.body: Use independent legal and technical review, record the agreed terms and understand the project’s responsibilities, protections and risks.
